title: Annotatio III §.VIII Rescript: Peace among Evangelicals our chief care; pulpits nearly free of mutual condemnations
pass_a_gloss: It is clear to You by what means, especially in the time of Our government, the highest care of promoting peace among Evangelicals has been Ours, by which also, with Divine Grace helping, we have so far progressed that in the Kingdom and the other Provinces subject to Our Empire those public bitternesses, imputations of heresies, and mutual condemnations of Protestants are scarcely any longer heard from the pulpit. Whence a sure hope shines upon us that Our pacific counsels, God blessing, will obtain a happy outcome.
pass_b_english: You know how, especially under Our reign, promoting peace among Evangelicals has been Our highest care —

and with God’s grace helping we have come so far that in the Kingdom and Our other subject provinces those public bitternesses, charges of heresy, and Protestants’ mutual condemnations are scarcely heard any longer from the pulpit.
So a sure hope shines on us that Our peace-counsels, God blessing them, will reach a happy end.
source_text: Perspectum Tibi est, quò pacto, Nostri praesertim regiminis tempore, pacis inter Evangelicos promovendae summa Nobis cura fuerit, qua etiam, adjuvante Divina Gratia, tantùm profecimus, ut in Regno caeterisque Imperio Nostro subjectis Provinciis publicae illae acerbitates, haeresium imputationes ac mutua Protestantium condemnationes vix ampliùs pro concione audiantur. Unde certa nobis spes affulget, pacifica Nostra consilia, benedicente Deo, felicem fortitura exitum.
notes: Peace progress under royal care; pulpits quieter.
